Publish from Maya#

**Status: 4.0.0-beta.1 — built and unit-tested, needs a real Maya install.** The plug-in's own code ran against a fake maya.cmds: which exporter it picks, the FBX flags, the units check, progress and Esc cancel, the menu and shelf commands, the settings and the drag installer. A GLB it exported (through the fake host) was published to a real local Verse server and finished (web/test/fix-verify-aec.mjs). Nothing has been run inside Maya yet.

Publish to Verse from a Verse menu and a Verse shelf: the scene — or the selection — is exported as GLB, uploaded with progress, and the share link is copied and opened. You get a link that opens on any phone.

You need: Maya 2022 or newer (Python 3). Windows, macOS or Linux.

1. Install#

Download VersePublish-Maya-4.0.0-beta.1.zip from the downloads page once the packages are published, or build it:

Code
sh integrations/aec/maya/make_package.sh   # -> integrations/aec/maya/dist/VersePublish-Maya-4.0.0-beta.1.zip

Unzip somewhere stable and **drag drag_to_install.py onto a Maya viewport**. It writes VersePublish.mod into your Maya modules folder (pointing at the unzipped folder), adds the Verse menu and shelf now, and scripts/userSetup.py adds them again at every start. To uninstall, delete the .mod file the install dialog names.

2. Server and key#

Verse ▸ Verse settings… — server URL (default https://verse.ctruh.com), API key, account token (from Studio), bake lighting, open the link when done. Tick Use … for every Verse plug-in to share server, key and token with SketchUp, Revit, Rhino, Cinema 4D, Houdini and the rest.

Nothing is compiled in. Settings live in the per-user settings.json every Verse plug-in shares (%APPDATA%\Ctruh\VersePublish\settings.json on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Ctruh/VersePublish/settings.json on macOS, ~/.config/ctruh/verse-publish/settings.json on Linux), maya section. VERSE_SERVER, VERSE_API_KEY, VERSE_TOKEN override it.

3. Publish#

  1. Verse ▸ Publish to Verse (or the shelf button), or **Publish selection to Verse**.
  2. Maya's progress window shows uploading % → building stages. Esc cancels and tells you whether anything was published.
  3. Published! — the link is on the clipboard and opens in the browser.

Success looks like: Published! with the link (also on the clipboard, and opened in the browser); a 250 cm cube measures 2.5 m in the viewer.

Files over 100 MB use the resumable upload: a dropped connection continues where the server got to.

What gets exported#

  • GLB, when a glTF exporter is registered with Maya (File ▸ Export All ▸ Files of type lists glTF / GLB). Maya does not ship one in every version; the plug-in uses any translator with "glTF" or "GLB" in its name and tries to load the common ones quietly.
  • Otherwise FBX with embedded textures, through Maya's own fbxmaya plug-in, converted to metres and Y-up; the server converts it — Upload FBX and OBJ.
  • Units. Maya works in centimetres by default and glTF is metres. The plug-in measures the exported GLB against the scene's bounding box: if the exporter wrote the raw centimetre numbers, the scene is wrapped in one root node scaled to metres (no vertex is changed); if it already wrote metres, the file is left alone. A 250 cm cube measures 2.5 m in the link.
  • Arnold / V-Ray shaders are not glTF materials; use Standard Surface or aiStandardSurface with plain textures for the best match.

Troubleshooting#

Every problem ends in one sentence; the first words tell you which row applies.

You seeWhat it meansDo this
"Could not reach the Verse server at …"Wrong server URL, no internet, or a firewall / proxy blocking the plug-in.Check Server URL in Verse ▸ Verse settings… (default https://verse.ctruh.com) and open it in a browser.
"The Verse server at … did not recognise the account token …"The token is mistyped, was revoked, or belongs to another server. Nothing was uploaded.Copy the token again from Studio, or clear it to publish without an account.
"The server did not accept your API key or account token …"This server only takes uploads with an API key; the sentence ends with its reason.Enter the key from the server's operator in Verse ▸ Verse settings….
"Upload limit reached: …"The hourly upload limit, or the API key's daily quota.Wait as the sentence says, or add an account token from Studio (a higher limit).
"The server is busy right now. …" / "The server is out of storage. …"The server's build queue or disk is full. Your file is fine.Publish again in a few minutes.
"The upload kept failing …"The connection dropped again and again.Publish again when the connection is steady; a large upload continues where it stopped.
"Verse cannot build … files yet. Export the model as GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that file instead."STEP / IGES / native CAD files are not built by the server yet.Export GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that.
"Stopped waiting for the server. The scene is still being built …"You cancelled after the upload; the server keeps building.The scene appears in your Verse dashboard (with an account token) when it is ready.
No Verse menu after a restartThe Maya module written by drag_to_install.py is missing or moved.Drag drag_to_install.py onto a viewport again from the folder you keep.
"There is no geometry to publish."No mesh in the scene (or the selection has none).Select meshes or their groups, then publish again.

Anything else: send the whole sentence (and, for a build error, the scene name) to hello@ctruh.com.

A GLB exported through the plug-in published to a real local server, scene donetested
The FBX road to the servertested when the gate machine has Blender (the server converts FBX with it)
